candidates.title: The Roof That Whistled
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered a high whistle from the school roof interrupted every outdoor lesson before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they shut the classroom windows, but the whistle continued whenever a breeze rose; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a loose roof vent had a narrow gap that made the wind sing through it; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they secured the vent from a safe maintenance platform and brought the class back outside, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The False Lighthouse Flash
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered a lighthouse signal flashed toward the harbor at the wrong intervals before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they replaced the lamp timer but the confusing flashes continued; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a loose mirror on the outer railing was reflecting each beam twice; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they secured the mirror and tested the signal from the harbor, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Orchard's Missing Row
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the orchard map led workers to an empty planting row before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they measured from the old fence but the trees still seemed missing; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized the boundary fence had been moved after a flood; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they located the original stone markers and corrected the map, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
